description: Mins Solutions: Building a astronaut health monitoring dashboard. Looking for UI/UX designers, data scientists, and pitch/video creators to complete our team. Join us to build a winning MVP!
summary: Mins-Health is an autonomous, offline-first clinical monitoring and triage platform designed for astronauts on deep space missions (Moon and Mars). During deep space exploration, Earth-Mars communication delays of 4 to 24 minutes render real-time telemedicine impossible. Furthermore, microgravity alters human basal physiology, causing conventional terrestrial medical monitors to trigger dangerous false alarms and induce crew alarm fatigue
details:
What It Does & How It Works Mins-Health is an autonomous flight medical cockpit engineered to safeguard astronaut health without relying on real-time ground control. Because deep space radio latency reaches up to 44 minutes round-trip, the platform runs 100% client-side with offline-first persistence (Zustand + localStorage), recovering full telemetry and medical baselines in under 15 ms after power disruptions.

Its flight decision core operates through four sequential modules:

  1. Personalized L-30 Baseline Engine: Microgravity induces cephalic fluid shifts and cardiovascular deconditioning. Instead of using terrestrial averages, the engine calculates each astronaut's individual 30-day pre-flight mean, unbiased standard deviation, and live Z-scores ($Z = (x - \mu)/\sigma$).
  2. Explainable Clinical Rules Engine: Strictly decouples mild statistical deviations ($\vert{}Z\vert{} \ge 1.4\sigma$, flagged as Watch/Caution for crew self-management) from absolute clinical breaches defined by NASA-STD-3001, which exclusively trigger critical ground escalation. Missing sensor channels are strictly isolated as NO_DATA (neutral gray) and never masked as nominal.
  3. HRP Hazard Synergy Causal Graph: Evaluates NASA's 5 Human Research Program (HRP) hazards (Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity, and Closed Environments). When multiple vitals shift simultaneously—such as tachycardia paired with elevated neutron dosimetry during a Solar Particle Event—the graph suppresses overlapping alerts and synthesizes a unified emergency protocol (e.g., deploying polyethylene shielding and moving to the water-shielded storm shelter).
  4. Aerospace SBAR Handover Packet: Automatically compiles standardized Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation (SBAR) telemetry packets signed with an Aerospace CRC32 checksum to prevent data corruption from cosmic-ray single-event upsets (SEUs) during Deep Space Network transmission.

Tools, Coding Languages & Technologies Used

  • Frontend & Architecture: Next.js / React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Zustand (offline-first state persistence).
  • 3D Visualization & Shaders: Three.js / WebGL (AstronautGLBViewer) featuring an interactive 3D spacesuit with a holographic X-ray shader, clickable anatomical hotspots (Helmet, Chest, Arm, Abdomen), and dynamic rim lighting reflecting real-time triage status.
  • Human-Factors Design: Built following MIL-STD-1472 and NASA-STD-3001 ergonomics using a zero-scroll 3-zone cockpit layout, tabular monospace numerals to eliminate visual jitter, and a high-contrast dark-space palette (#0B0C10) to prevent ocular fatigue.

Creativity, Considerations & Intended Impact Rather than building a passive dashboard, our team designed an active clinical decision-support copilot that directly combats alarm fatigue and cognitive overload in high-stress environments. By validating our thresholds against real commercial spaceflight multi-omics data (NASA OSDR OSD-575), Mins-Health bridges space medicine standards with modern aerospace software engineering, providing a scalable foundation for Artemis lunar missions, Mars transit, and remote terrestrial telemedicine.
